title: Deductions from Gross Total Income — Chapter VI-A

content.overview: Deductions from gross total income are Chapter VI-A. They are applied after set-off of loss and after the heads are computed. They are not business expenses and not exemptions. The deduction is the lowest of the amount paid, the section limit and the gross total income. Order matters. A Chapter VI-A claim does not reduce a head before set-off.

cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.

cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.

enhancement.definition: Deductions from gross total income are Chapter VI-A. They are applied after set-off of loss and after the heads are computed. They are not business expenses and not exemptions. The deduction is the lowest of the amount paid, the section limit and the gross total income.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Order matters. A Chapter VI-A claim does not reduce a head before set-off.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The chapter is a code of deductions. Section 80C is savings. Section 80D is health cover. Section 80G is donations, some with a qualifying limit. A payment that is also claimed as a business expense cannot be deducted again. The return must contain the claim where the Act requires it.
examples: Health-insurance premium is claimed under section 80D.
The same premium is not also put into section 80C.
A loss is set off before the deduction.
